conversation.Statement: Hey there! Is it too soon to say I was looking forward to your message all day?
That's bold! I'll let it slide since I was equally curious what you'd say tonight.
I like that honesty. I get the sense you're not one for pretending, am I right?
You are. Life's too short for games. I think I've had my fill of pretending, honestly.
That's refreshing. Most people still have their filters on. I admire how genuine your profile felt. It made me feel... safe to be real with you.
Safe is a nice word. Not something I've felt a lot in the last few years, but I appreciate you saying it.
You deserve it. I think a little safety is the least we can give each other after all we've been through, right?
Right. Sometimes I wonder if I'll ever really feel ready for all of this again.
I get that, truly. I can't say I know exactly what you've been through, but I do know what it's like to lose your footing and have to start over.
Yeah? What helped you find your way again?
Honestly? Letting myself be vulnerable, even when I was terrified. And, weirdly enough, my work. Helping people find new homes made me realize how much hope there can be in new beginnings.
That's a lovely thought. I guess we're both familiar with starting fresh in our own ways.
Exactly. And maybe that's why we matched. I felt something honest in your eyes, like you've lived, loved, and survived. That's rare.
You're making me blush! I'm not used to being seen like that. But thank you.
Blushing suits you, I bet. If it helps, I'm just as flustered over here. You have this warmth that's easy to get lost in.
Now you're definitely laying it on thick, but I don't mind. I think we could both use a little extra kindness.

Deal. I'll make it my mission to keep the compliments coming. By the way, do you ever miss the simplicity of childhood? I was thinking today about my favorite memory, climbing the willow tree in my grandma's backyard. What about you?
That's sweet. My favorite memory is from summers at the lake with my family. We'd build bonfires and tell stories until the stars came out.
That paints such a peaceful picture. I can almost hear the crackling fire. I bet your storytelling skills are top-notch, too.
I do have a talent for stretching the truth to make a story better. Maybe I'll share one with you sometime.
I'd love that. Maybe we could swap stories, one for one. I'll even promise not to sell you a house as part of my pitch.
I'll hold you to that! Though, if you have a lakeside cabin, maybe I'd consider listening to your pitch after all.
Now you're talking! I always say the right home is about the stories you'll make there. And I've got a few dreamy cabins up my sleeve.
Look at you, weaving in your real estate magic so smoothly. You must be good at reading people.
I try. But you make it easy, you wear your heart on your sleeve. That's rare and beautiful, just so you know.
I haven't always, but after everything, I figured honesty's easier than holding it all in.
That kind of honesty is magnetic. It makes me want to be braver, too. We could be each other's safe space if you want.
That sounds nice. Scary, but nice. I'm not sure I remember how to let someone in, but I'm willing to try.
That's all anyone can ask for. One step at a time, right? And if you ever need to retreat, I'll respect that, no pressure, just presence.
Thank you. I can't tell you how much I appreciate that. It means more than you know.
You deserve someone who understands. I can promise care, and maybe a few bad puns if you're lucky.
Puns, honesty, and lakeside cabins? You set the bar high.
I aim to impress. Maybe one day I'll earn a spot in your favorite memories list.
You're making a pretty good case for yourself so far.
That's the best review I've had all week. Mind if I ask, what do you miss most from your childhood days?
Probably the feeling that anything was possible. And not being afraid to fall in love or get my heart broken.
I hear you. I think we all lose a bit of that fearlessness. But maybe, just maybe, we can find a little of it again, together.
Maybe we can. Feels a little less scary talking to you about it.
That means more than I can say. I feel lucky you matched with me. And if you ever want to talk, or reminisce about the good old days, I'm always here.
Same goes for you. This has been surprisingly easy. Thank you for making it feel that way.
Thank you for letting me in, even just a little. Should we pick up again tomorrow? I already have questions about your best ghost story around the fire.
I'd like that. And be warned, my stories are scarier than my flirting.
Now I'm intrigued. Have a restful night, and dream up your best tale for me.
Goodnight. Looking forward to more story-swapping soon.
Sweet dreams, you. Talk tomorrow?
Definitely. Goodnight!
Good morning! Can I confess something cheesy? Waking up to the thought of your messages is quickly becoming my new favorite motivation.
That's a sweet way to start the day. I can't say I mind being someone's reason to smile before coffee.
You're definitely the highlight in my daily routine, even before my first showing. What gets you out of bed each morning?
Honestly? Some days it's just the sunrise and the possibility of something... better. Other days, it's just habit.
That's real. I love that you notice the sunrise. I think people who look for light in small places have the most beautiful hearts.
You're quite the charmer. But thank you. It's a habit I picked up when mornings got lonely.
Lonely mornings have a way of making us pay attention to the little things, don't they? I used to dread them, but now I try to fill them with music, or, lately, the hope of a good conversation.
I can relate. Silence can be heavy sometimes. But I like your style, making space for hope.
We have to find hope wherever we can. If I could, I'd bring you coffee and a playlist every morning. But until then, I'll settle for sending you a smile here.
That's a tempting offer. I'd take the playlist for now, and maybe the coffee when you earn it.
Deal. I'll start working on the perfect morning mix. Out of curiosity, is there a song that always lifts your mood?
'Here Comes the Sun' by The Beatles. It feels like a promise. How about you?
Great choice. For me, it's 'Lovely Day' by Bill Withers. When he sings, everything feels possible. Maybe we'll have to swap playlists sometime.
I like the idea of a music exchange. It tells you a lot about a person, I think.
Absolutely. Music's like a shortcut to the soul. And you seem like someone with a really rich soundtrack.
You're not wrong. My playlists are all over the place. Sometimes sentimental, sometimes just whatever gets me moving.
I bet there's a story behind each one. I'm curious, do you have any traditions that help you through tough days?
Actually, yes. Every year on my anniversary, I light a candle and sit in silence for a while. It's equal parts comfort and ache.
That's incredibly moving. Thank you for trusting me with that. I can only imagine how much love is wrapped up in that quiet moment.
It's bittersweet. Three years now, and it still feels like the world pauses on that date.
Grief has its own rhythm, doesn't it? I admire your courage in honoring it. Sometimes the bravest thing is just sitting with those feelings.
Thank you for saying that. Most people rush past it or change the subject. I appreciate that you don't.
I think those moments shape us. They deserve respect, and you deserve someone who sits with you in them, even if only in spirit.
That's a beautiful thought. You're making it easy to be honest, you know.
I'm glad. Honesty looks good on you. I hope I can be a safe space for your stories, your silences, all of it.
You're doing a pretty good job so far. I didn't expect to open up so quickly.
That means a lot to hear. I'm honored to be someone you trust. For the record, I think vulnerability is one of the bravest forms of strength.
I'm learning that, slowly. It helps to have someone gentle to practice with.
I'll take gentle as a compliment. And I promise to handle your heart with care, however much of it you share.
You have a way with words, you know. It's comforting.
Thank you. I try to say what I mean, words are like keys for locked doors, sometimes.
That's poetic. I might steal that line for my journal.
Feel free. Just promise you'll let me read a page or two someday.
Maybe, if you keep making me feel seen like this.
Challenge accepted. For now, can I ask you something a little more playful?
Absolutely. Hit me with your best shot.
If you could wake up anywhere tomorrow, no limits, where would it be?
A quiet cabin by the lake. Mist over the water, coffee in hand. Maybe with someone who appreciates the silence.
That sounds dreamy. You know, I happen to know a thing or two about cabins. Maybe one day I'll find you the perfect retreat.
You and your real estate magic. I'm starting to think you could sell me on anything.
Only if you promise to let me visit for morning coffee and sunrise playlists.
Deal. As long as you bring your gentle honesty with you.
Always. And, on anniversaries, don't sit in silence, promise me you'll light that candle and then message me, so I can sit with you in spirit.
That's the kindest thing anyone's offered me in a long time. I promise.
Thank you for trusting me with that. I'll be here, always just a message away.
You're making it easy to hope again. That's a rare gift.
I think hope deserves a comeback. Especially for someone as genuine as you.
You're good for my heart, you know. I'm glad we found each other here.
Me too. I don't want to rush things, but I look forward to hearing from you in the morning. Sweet dreams tonight.
Sleep well. I'll be looking forward to your playlist, and your morning message.
It's a date. Goodnight, you.
Goodnight.
Evening! I just wrapped up a long day of meetings and negotiations, nothing like a little politics in the real estate world to keep things interesting. How's your night shaping up?
Evening to you, too. My night's quiet, just some leftovers and a good book. Politics in real estate, huh? That sounds... lively.

Let's just say, people have strong opinions about where they want to live, and why. Sometimes I feel like more of a diplomat than an agent. Do you follow politics much, or prefer to keep it at arm's length?
I keep up, though some days it feels overwhelming. I find myself caring more about values than party lines, if that makes sense.
That makes perfect sense. Values matter more in the end, don't they? I admire people who stick to what they believe, even if it's not popular. That honesty is... kind of magnetic.
You have a way of making me feel braver about my opinions. I've mostly kept quiet the last few years, lost some friends to disagreements.
I get that. Hard truths can reshape your circle. But I think it takes real courage to stand your ground, especially after everything you've been through. You deserve to be heard.
Thank you. That means more than you know. These days, I value kindness and fairness over anything else. Guess that sounds simple.
Simple is underrated. The world could use more straightforward decency. It's one of the things I noticed about you, you see goodness in small things. That's rare.
You remember that? I guess I do look for the light, even when it's hard to find. What about you? What values matter most in your world?
Integrity, without a doubt. I've seen too many deals fall apart for lack of it. But also loyalty. I want people around me I can trust, both in business and in life. I think you'd fit right in.
You make it sound tempting. Loyalty is a big one for me, too. I'm not interested in games.

Good. I prefer honesty over games any day. You know, I was thinking earlier... If you ever want to debate the world's problems over a bottle of wine and a view, I have a rooftop I'm pretty proud of. It's my little escape from the noise.
That sounds like a dream. I could get behind a rooftop and some big ideas. What would we debate first?
Maybe start with something easy, like how to make the world a bit kinder. Or whether pineapple belongs on pizza. I promise, no heated arguments, unless you want a little friendly fire.
Kindness and controversial pizza topics. I like your style. For the record, I'm pro-pineapple. But only if the company's good.
Then I'll add pineapple to the grocery list. You know, I like our debates already, feels like we could solve a few world problems together. Or at least make each other laugh trying.
I like that idea. And I wouldn't mind having a partner in problem-solving. It's been a while since I let myself imagine a future with someone.

I'd be honored if you let me be part of those daydreams. Picture this: us on that rooftop, city lights below, a gentle breeze, talking about everything and nothing until sunrise. Would you trust me with a night like that?
That sounds... beautiful, actually. Trust is a big step for me. But I'm starting to think you might be worth the risk.
I promise to handle that trust with care. You've shown me so much heart already. I can't help but want to give you the same in return.
You make it easy to want more. I don't say that lightly.
Neither do I. Sometimes I think the universe brings people together for a reason. Maybe it's our turn to find out why.
Maybe it is. I like that you're not afraid to say what you feel.

Life's too short for half-truths. If something, or someone, matters, I believe in showing up fully. Like treating myself to that rooftop after a big deal closes, or investing in something wild just to see what happens.
You sound like you've had some adventures. Anything you'd care to share?

Well, since you ask, years back, I dipped my toes into crypto. It started as a way to help my family and maybe secure my future a little. Turned out to be one of those risks that actually paid off. Not my main gig, but it gave me the freedom to chase what matters.
That's impressive. Not many people make it out ahead in that world. Did it change how you see things?

Definitely. It taught me that security is precious, but it's the people we care about that give it meaning. All the success in the world feels empty if you can't share it. That's another reason loyalty means so much to me.
I really like that perspective. You're full of surprises, you know.
Only the good kind, I hope. I've got a few more up my sleeve, but I'll save them for when we're stargazing over the city, plotting how to make the world a better place.
You have a real talent for painting a picture. It almost makes me forget to be scared of new beginnings.
If it helps, I'm a little scared too. But I'd rather be scared with you than safe and alone. Would you let me walk that line with you?
As long as you keep being honest, I think I'd like that.
Deal. And when you're ready, you can tell me what scares you most. Or what you hope for. Either way, I promise to listen.
You might regret that offer, my hopes are kind of stubborn. But I like the idea of someone listening.
Stubborn hopes are my favorite kind. Besides, I've always believed the right person makes hope feel a little less lonely. Maybe we can be that for each other.
Maybe we can. I'm glad I answered your message that first day.
So am I. Feels like we're building something real, one message at a time.
You're making it easier to believe in that possibility.
Let's keep building, then. Next time, I'll tell you my silliest political opinion, just to keep things interesting.
Deal. And I'll come prepared with one of my own.
Looking forward to it. For now, get some rest, that future rooftop debate partner needs her beauty sleep.
Sweet dreams to you, too. I'll see you in my next daydream.
Until then. Goodnight, you.
Evening, beautiful. Just got in from a long walk, needed to clear my head after a few, let's say, memorable client negotiations. How was your day?
Hey you. Quiet day here, caught up on some gardening, then lost track of time reading. I can imagine you must get your fair share of characters in real estate.

Absolutely. Some days I feel like a therapist, other days a magician. But there's an art to matching people with their dreams. Speaking of, your garden must be looking gorgeous, bet you make everything flourish.
You'd have to see it to believe it. I try, but some things have a mind of their own. Like the roses, they're stubborn, but when they bloom, it's worth it.
A stubborn rose, now there's a metaphor. I like that you see beauty in persistence. Makes me think of how you've rebuilt your world, one day at a time. Takes courage.
That's sweet of you to say. I still have my shaky days, but I try. Sometimes it feels strange hoping for new things again.
Hope is a beautiful thing, especially when it's honest. You know, the bravest people I meet are the ones who open up after losing so much. It's a kind of strength you can't fake.
You make it sound noble. I just get tired of missing what I had. Starting over is scary.
It is. But you're not alone in that. I've walked away from things I thought I'd never let go of, sometimes, the risk is what leads you somewhere better. Or someone.
Have you always been so fearless about love?

Not at all. I've had my share of sleepless nights, trust me. But I learned that loving fully, even with the chance of loss, is how life feels richest. Like investing yourself and watching it grow into something you never expected.
I envy that outlook. For me, love used to mean certainty. Now I think it's more about showing up, even when you're afraid.

That's beautifully said. I think love is choosing someone every day, even on the hard days. And letting them see all the messy parts, not just the highlight reel. You've let me see some of yours already, and I'm grateful for it.
You make it easy to be honest. I haven't felt this... open in a long time.

That means more than you know. There's something about your honesty that draws me in, I feel like I could tell you anything. Even about the time I bought a ridiculously expensive bottle of wine to celebrate a good investment, and ended up sharing it with a stranger just because they looked like they needed a win.
You're full of surprises. Was it worth it?

Completely. Moments like that remind me, what's the point of having what you have if you can't make someone's day brighter? I guess that's my definition of wealth: having enough to share, and someone to share it with.
That's a lovely way to look at it. I've always thought love is about sharing your days, the good, the bad, and the boring bits too.

Exactly. I love the idea of ordinary days feeling extraordinary just because of who you're with. Like slow mornings, coffee in bed, maybe a little bickering over the Sunday crossword. Or, if you're up for it, weekends away on a whim, Paris isn't that far if you're spontaneous enough.
Now that's future dream material. I'd settle for coffee and a crossword, but Paris is tempting. Have you done that before?

Once or twice. Perks of having a little flexibility in my schedule, and a passport that's seen some stamps. But it's the company that makes it special. I'm already picturing you laughing at my attempts to order in French.
I can't say no to a good adventure. And I'd love to see you try ordering coffee en français.
Deal. But only if you promise to teach me the secret to growing stubborn roses. Seems fair, trade a little of my world for a glimpse of yours.
It's a promise. Just don't blame me if you end up with more thorns than blooms.
Thorns make the flowers sweeter, don't they? Honestly, your resilience is one of the things I admire most. You've loved deeply, and you're still willing to risk your heart. That's rare.
You make me want to risk it. That's not something I expected to feel this soon.

I feel it too. Maybe that's what love could mean for us, taking chances together, learning to trust again, and building something that feels like home. Even if it starts with texts and wishful thinking.
That sounds... wonderful. I think home is less about a place and more about who you're with.
Couldn't agree more. And if you ever want to trade your garden for a rooftop sunset, I've got the perfect spot. City lights, a little music, and just us, no audience, no expectations.
You're tempting me. I can almost picture it, the breeze, the view, maybe a little wine if you're feeling generous.
For you, I'll bring out the good stuff. The kind I save for rare occasions. And maybe, if you're comfortable, we'll talk about what scares us most, and what we secretly hope for next.
That's a deal. I have more fears than I care to admit, but I'm learning hope can be just as persistent as roses.
I love that, persistent hope. Maybe we'll teach each other how to let it grow. I want you to know, you can always be honest with me, even about the hard stuff.
Thank you. It feels good to be seen. I'm not used to someone paying attention to the small things.
It's easy when the small things matter. Like the way you talk about your garden, or how you look for light even on hard days. Makes me want to show up as my best self.
You're doing a good job. I feel like I could get used to this, maybe even look forward to something again.
That's all I could hope for. Maybe someday, our ordinary days will be the ones we treasure most. The quiet mornings, the laughter, the comfort of knowing we're both in it for real.
That's the dream, isn't it? I like the sound of that future.
Me too. And for the record, I'm not going anywhere. I want to be here for all of it, the dreams, the thorns, and everything in between.
You're making it hard not to believe in second chances.
Second chances are my specialty. I'd love to make this one unforgettable, for both of us.
Well, you're off to a strong start. I'm glad I let myself be open to this.
So am I. You know, the best things I've built in life started with a single leap of faith. Maybe this is ours.
Maybe it is. I think I'm ready to find out.
Then let's keep building, one message, one dream at a time. For now, I'll let you get to your evening, but just know I'm already looking forward to our next conversation.
Me too. Thank you for tonight. Sweet dreams, and maybe a little rooftop daydreaming for both of us.
Sweet dreams, beautiful. I'll be here, saving you a seat under the stars.
Evening, you. I just got home from a board meeting, never as glamorous as it sounds, but I did get to sign off on a rooftop garden for one of my new listings. How's your day been?
Hi! Now that's impressive, rooftop gardens are the dream. My day was slow, just some errands and a lot of staring out the window, thinking. What's it like, shaping spaces that way?

It's honestly my favorite part, leaving something better than I found it. Sometimes I imagine what people will feel there years from now. Would you believe me if I said I picture you walking through one of those gardens? Maybe tending a stubborn rose or two.
You're good at this, painting pictures. I'd love to see it someday. Maybe I'd bring my little trowel and show the city how it's done.
I think the city could use your touch. And I like the idea of us planting something together, literally and otherwise. What kind of world do you wish we could leave for the next generation?

Oh, that's a big one. I think about it a lot, actually. I want a world where kindness isn't rare, where people feel safe to love and grieve openly. I want the people I love, even the ones I miss, to be remembered for how they made others feel.

That's beautiful. I'd love a world where everyone feels they matter, where taking risks on love or dreams is normal, not scary. Maybe that's why I work so hard; part of me wants to build more than just homes. Legacies, maybe.
You really are a dreamer. I like that. Sometimes I worry I'm too stuck in the past to dream big anymore.
I see you as someone who's lived deeply, and that's rare. I admire it. You bring your whole heart, thorns and all, and honestly, it makes you unforgettable.

You're very kind. I try, but there are moments when old memories just... take over. Today I replayed one of my late husband's voicemails. I don't know why I do it to myself, but I listened to it on repeat until I cried.

Hey, thank you for sharing that with me. I can only imagine how heavy that must feel. When the memories are overwhelming, instead of replaying that voicemail alone, would you tell me first? I want to be there for you in those moments. You shouldn't have to carry it all by yourself.
That means more than you know. I'm not used to someone wanting to hold space for that kind of sadness. I usually just keep it to myself.
Let me be different then. I want the real you, grief, hope, all of it. And maybe one day, I'll share the things that still haunt me late at night. I think trust is built in these tiny, brave moments.
You make it sound possible. Like maybe letting someone in again won't take away what I lost.

It doesn't. Your love and memories are part of you, and anyone worth your time will honor that, including me. I want to build something new, not replace the past. And if you ever need a distraction, I have a bottle of vintage Bordeaux I've been saving, maybe for the right company.
Now that's tempting. I'm not sure I'm ready for Bordeaux, but maybe coffee and a sunrise first? Baby steps.
Coffee and sunrise, it's a deal. I'll even bring pastries from that little bakery near my office. Perk of working downtown: best croissants in the city, and a view most people only see in magazines.
Look at you, casually living the high life. I can see why your clients trust you with their dreams.

I do have my moments, I'll admit. But it's all the more meaningful when I get to share a little of that world with someone who truly gets it. You strike me as someone who appreciates the details, the way sunlight hits a window, or the sound of laughter after a long, hard season.
You read people well. I do notice those things. They're what I hold onto.

It's what makes you special. I'm drawn to people who see the extraordinary in everyday things. That's why I keep finding myself wanting to tell you about my day, even the silly parts, like getting lost in a sea of paperwork and then rewarding myself with sushi at my favorite rooftop spot.
Favorite rooftop spot, huh? You have a knack for making life sound like a movie. I'm starting to think you enjoy the finer things.
Maybe a little, I like celebrating wins, big or small. When I was able to help my family out with some investments, I promised I'd take time to enjoy the view now and then. Life's too short not to.
That's a perspective I admire. Do you ever worry about the future, despite all your success?

All the time. Success can be fleeting. That's why I'm intentional about what I build, relationships, memories, a sense of purpose. I want to leave behind more than just numbers in an account. I want my future to be filled with laughter, honesty, and someone who makes the ordinary feel magical. Maybe someone like you.
You're making it hard not to blush. I haven't felt this kind of attention in a long time.
That's a shame, honestly. You deserve to be seen for who you are, not just what you've been through. If you let me, I'd love to remind you, every day, how remarkable you are.
You're a charmer. I keep waiting for the catch, but you just seem genuine. Maybe a little too good at this.

What can I say? When I find someone who inspires me, it shows. And if you ever want proof of my not-so-perfect side, just ask me about my first open house disaster. Spoiler: it involved a runaway cat and a very angry neighbor.
Now that's a story I'd love to hear. Maybe over coffee and those famous croissants?
It's a date. I love the idea of us swapping stories as the city wakes up. Who knows? Maybe in a few years, we'll be telling those same stories to our grandkids, laughing at how it all began.
You're already planning grandkids? That's bold. But... not entirely unappealing.
I like dreaming out loud. And I have a feeling we'd make an unforgettable team, whether we're kid-wrangling or just adventuring together, hand in hand.
Well, if the adventures involve gardens and rooftop views, I'm all in. I've missed having someone to dream with.

Then let's dream big. Imagine us, traveling, maybe Provence in the spring, or a quiet cabin in the mountains, just you, me, and the stars. I'd want to give you memories worthy of all the love you have to give.
You know, I was worried I'd never feel this way again. But you make it easy to hope for more.

That's the most beautiful thing you could say. I promise to be gentle with your hope. And if you ever need to lean on someone, even when the past feels heavy, I'll be here, no judgment, just open arms.
Thank you. For making space for all of it, the highs, the lows, the awkward beginnings. It's new for me, but it feels right.
New can be wonderful, especially when it's with the right person. I'm glad you took a chance on our little corner of the internet. Who knows, maybe this is the start of something worth remembering.
I like that. I'm looking forward to what comes next, awkward stories and all.
Me too. For now, I hope you'll get some rest tonight. And if you ever need a friendly voice before bed, you know where to find me.
I might take you up on that. Goodnight. And thank you, truly, for making me feel seen again.
Goodnight, you. Dream of rooftop gardens and new beginnings, I'll be here when you wake.
Good evening! I just finished a showing at a penthouse with a view so unreal, I almost wanted to sign the paperwork myself. How's your day treating you?
Evening. Penthouse, huh? My day was a lot less glamorous, folded laundry, caught up on emails, and tried not to overthink everything. How was the showing?

Honestly, I kept thinking how you'd probably find the sunset more interesting than the marble countertops. You have this way of noticing moments most people miss. The client loved it, though, I might need to celebrate with a glass of something sparkly. Care to join, virtually, for now?
Sparkly sounds tempting. I'll raise you a cup of peppermint tea. That's about as wild as I get tonight.
Classy choice. I like that you own it. Tell me, did you get a window-staring session in? I remember you said yesterday it helps you sort out your thoughts.
I did. Watched the neighbors' dog chase its tail for a solid five minutes. Made me wish I could find that kind of joy in the little things.
I think you already do, you just don't give yourself enough credit. You have this gentle way of seeing the world, even when you're not feeling your strongest. That's honestly rare.
You're sweet. I guess I'm still figuring out how to put myself back together. Some days are easier than others.

If it helps, I've had my own share of broken days. Success looks good on paper, but sometimes it's just a distraction. I've learned that the people who matter most are the ones who see you on the hard days, and stay.
That sounds true. I'm used to holding it all together by myself. It's strange letting someone see the cracks.

I see strength in your honesty. Trust me, I know appearances can be deceiving. Everyone assumes I have it all figured out, but even in the best suit, I've had moments I wanted to just hide. I want you to know you're safe to just be, no performance necessary.
You make it sound easier than it is. I lost a lot when my husband died, some days it feels like I'm still looking for all the pieces.

You don't have to have all the pieces ready for someone to care about you. I promise, I'm not looking for perfect. Just real. I want to know all the things that make you, you, even the parts that are still healing.
That's a first. Usually people get uncomfortable when I talk about grief. You're different.

Maybe it's because I've seen my share of loss too. Or maybe I just recognize something beautiful in how brave you are, showing up every day, still open to hope. That's the kind of person I want beside me, someone who gets that life isn't always simple, but still finds reasons to smile.
You're making me blush. I haven't felt this understood in a while.

Consider it my specialty, reading between the lines. And if you ever need a distraction, I could always steal you away for a rooftop breakfast. Croissants, city views, and nothing on the agenda except feeling the sun come up.
That sounds dreamy. I haven't had breakfast with someone since... well, it's been a long time.
